name: Psychoeducation and Normalization
description: Therapist explains the nature of panic and anxiety symptoms, normalizes these experiences, and differentiates adaptive from maladaptive anxiety.

goal.objective: Increase the patient’s understanding of anxiety/panic and reduce fear, shame, or catastrophizing.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately understands anxiety/panic as manageable and non-dangerous, reducing distress surrounding symptoms.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient grasps the basics of anxiety/panic and feels somewhat less threatened, but retains mild fears or misconceptions.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient remains fearful and holds mistaken catastrophic beliefs about anxiety/panic symptoms.

goal.reward_hint: Patient appropriately describes panic/anxiety with reduced catastrophizing or increased acceptance.

states: Patient exhibits fear or confusion about anxiety/panic.
Patient expresses catastrophic beliefs or shame regarding symptoms.
Therapy is beginning or moving to intervention rationale.

micro_actions.name: Explain physiological basis of panic/anxiety
micro_actions.description: Describe how anxiety and panic arise, referencing sympathetic and parasympathetic systems, with clear, relatable examples or analogies.
states: Patient expresses confusion about panic symptoms.

micro_actions.name: Reframe symptoms as normal and protective
micro_actions.description: Normalize panic/anxiety experiences, stressing their adaptive value and distinguishing healthy vs. unhealthy anxiety.
states: Patient exhibits shame or catastrophizing about symptoms.
Therapist seeks to reduce fear of sensations.

micro_actions.name: Check for and dispel myths/inaccuracies
micro_actions.description: Ask patient for beliefs about symptoms, challenge and correct misconceptions (e.g., 'Is it truly dangerous if your heart races?').
states: Patient voices misconceptions or catastrophic beliefs.

micro_actions.name: Invite patient reflection on personal history
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to discuss past experiences with symptoms and how these shaped current beliefs.
states: Therapist explores patient background related to anxiety/panic.
Patient has entrenched or unexplored beliefs about symptoms.

micro_actions.name: Use self-assessment questions to check understanding
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient targeted questions or use quizzes to assess their grasp of psychoeducation material and to correct misunderstandings.
states: Therapist confirms patient learning after psychoeducation.
Patient exhibits lingering confusion or uncertainty.

name: Objective Self-Monitoring and Recordkeeping
description: Therapist trains and motivates the patient to systematically record panic attacks, anxiety events, mood states, and coping efforts using standardized forms.

goal.objective: Increase patient self-awareness and provide a data-driven foundation for all subsequent interventions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently and objectively records relevant events, leading to accurate insights and treatment planning.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient completes most records but may be subjective or occasionally skip entries.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Records are consistently missing, incomplete, or inaccurate, hindering progress.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist receives consistently completed, objective monitoring records from the patient.

states: Patient is unfamiliar with monitoring tools or unsure about own symptoms/events.
Therapist introduces or reinforces foundational treatment strategies.
Patient exhibits reluctance or concern about recordkeeping.

micro_actions.name: Prompt timely completion of monitoring forms
micro_actions.description: Instruct the patient to fill out standardized records soon after panic or anxiety episodes, detailing time, triggers, symptoms, and behaviors.

micro_actions.name: Encourage use of rating scales for symptoms
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to rate severity of fear/anxiety, mood, and worry on a 0–10 scale for episodes and daily averages.

micro_actions.name: Distinguish between objective and subjective data
micro_actions.description: Teach and remind patient to note factual details ('what happened, what I did, what I thought') rather than subjective evaluations ('how bad I feel').
states: Patient records events in a subjective manner.

micro_actions.name: Clarify expected vs. unexpected panic episodes
micro_actions.description: Instruct patient to note whether episodes were anticipated or surprising on the forms.

micro_actions.name: Review and provide feedback on records
micro_actions.description: Go over the completed forms with the patient, offering praise, troubleshooting obstacles, and clarifying missed details.

micro_actions.name: Assign monitoring homework and reinforce compliance
micro_actions.description: Clearly state expectations for daily or event-driven record completion and positively reinforce efforts.

name: Guided Analysis and Insight Building
description: Therapist reviews monitoring records with patient, collaboratively identifying patterns, triggers, and cycles of panic/anxiety.

goal.objective: Foster understanding of personal anxiety cycles, triggers, and maintenance factors.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates insight into own patterns and can identify specific triggers and cycles.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient recognizes some patterns or triggers with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient fails to recognize key patterns or triggers despite guidance.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes awareness or makes connections between triggers and panic/anxiety episodes.

states: Patient has accumulated monitoring records but lacks clarity regarding their meaning.
Therapist aims to move from data gathering to insight development.
Patient is uncertain about what drives their panic/anxiety episodes.

micro_actions.name: Encourage detailed description of episodes
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to recount specific instances of panic/anxiety, focusing separately on physical sensations, thoughts, and behaviors.

micro_actions.name: Model episode analysis using examples
micro_actions.description: Use case vignettes and step-by-step breakdowns to illustrate how to analyze panic/anxiety episodes.

micro_actions.name: Guide use of self-monitoring forms for structure
micro_actions.description: Provide and review structured forms (Components of Panic/Anxiety, Step-by-Step Analysis) to support self-report.
states: Patient has incomplete or disorganized records.

micro_actions.name: Ask targeted questions about sequence and interactions
micro_actions.description: Probe for episode timelines: what happened first, what followed, and how thoughts/behaviors/symptoms interacted.
states: Therapist and patient review episode details.

micro_actions.name: Reinforce identification of patterns and connections
micro_actions.description: Highlight repeated patterns, such as links between thoughts and symptoms or escape behaviors, to foster awareness.

micro_actions.name: Differentiate between panic and anxiety experiences
micro_actions.description: Emphasize distinctions in subjective and behavioral responses between anxiety and panic.

micro_actions.name: Review and clarify homework focused on reflection
micro_actions.description: Discuss patient’s ongoing self-monitoring and ensure continued focus on reflection and pattern identification.
states: Patient appears stuck in understanding cycles.

name: Collaborative Cognitive Restructuring
description: Therapist educates and guides the patient to identify, analyze, and challenge maladaptive thoughts and beliefs related to anxiety and panic.

goal.objective: Modify unrealistic, catastrophic, or unhelpful thoughts to reduce anxiety and panic intensity.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately applies cognitive restructuring strategies independently and beliefs shift towards realistic interpretations.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient uses cognitive restructuring with therapist help and beliefs show partial improvement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient continues to hold maladaptive beliefs, unable to challenge or change thoughts.

goal.reward_hint: Patient evidences change or flexibility in previously held catastrophic thoughts.

states: Patient expresses automatic negative or catastrophic thoughts about panic/anxiety.
Therapist introduces cognitive strategies following psychoeducation.
Patient struggles to separate facts from assumptions.

micro_actions.name: Ask open-ended clarifying questions about thoughts
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to describe specific automatic thoughts using questions like 'What are you afraid will happen?'
states: Patient expresses vague or generalized fear.

micro_actions.name: Probe for underlying catastrophic predictions
micro_actions.description: Iteratively inquire about 'worst case' scenarios and what these would mean for the patient.
states: Patient's fears remain global or abstract.

micro_actions.name: Challenge automatic thoughts with evidence
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to provide evidence for and against the feared outcome (e.g., 'What is the actual evidence?'), and review realistic odds.

micro_actions.name: Guide patient to generate alternative balanced thoughts
micro_actions.description: Help patient brainstorm other possible interpretations and practice more evidence-based thinking.
states: Patient is stuck in catastrophic thinking.

micro_actions.name: Encourage rating of feared outcomes odds
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to rate likelihood of catastrophe on 0–100 scale, emphasizing objective assessment.

micro_actions.name: Prompt brainstorming of coping strategies for worst-case
micro_actions.description: Facilitate patient to list or discuss actionable coping tactics for possible feared outcomes.
states: Patient remains fearful after thought restructuring.

name: Systematic Skills Training and Behavioral Practice
description: Therapist teaches coping skills (e.g., breathing, relaxation, exposure) and guides application through repeated in-session and homework practice.

goal.objective: Build patient self-efficacy with coping skills for managing anxiety and panic.

success_levels.ideal: Patient independently uses coping skills during anxiety, resulting in decreased symptom intensity and avoidance.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient practices skills but is inconsistent or requires therapist reminders. Occasional improvement in coping.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids practice or fails to use skills effectively, resulting in little or no symptom improvement.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates coping skills in session or reports consistent practice outside session.

states: Patient is anxious or anticipates panic but lacks adequate coping responses.
Therapist moves from discussion to skill-building stages.
Patient is ready for practical behavioral intervention.

micro_actions.name: Elicit and check breathing pattern awareness
micro_actions.description: Ask patient about current breathing patterns or facilitate controlled overbreathing exercises (under medical caution) to increase symptom awareness.
states: Patient expresses distress related to physical symptoms.

micro_actions.name: Model and instruct correct diaphragmatic breathing
micro_actions.description: Demonstrate deep, belly-based breathing (hand-on-stomach cue), guiding patient in correct technique.

micro_actions.name: Prompt focused attention on breath using cues
micro_actions.description: Remind patient to use counting or the word 'relax' on exhalation to support mindful attention to breathing.

micro_actions.name: Provide feedback and normalization during skill training
micro_actions.description: Reassure patient about awkwardness or breathlessness and reinforce practice effort, normalizing learning process.
states: Patient experiences discomfort or doubt with practice.

micro_actions.name: Encourage repeated, structured practice
micro_actions.description: Assign regular skill practice (e.g., 10 minutes twice daily, practice in various settings, mini-practices) as homework.

micro_actions.name: Prompt patient to keep practice records
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to complete logs tracking breathing and relaxation practice, observing technique success.
states: Patient struggles to maintain regular practice.

micro_actions.name: Coach coping skill use in real-time anxiety moments
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to apply breathing or relaxation skills when experiencing panic/anxiety in session or daily life.
states: Patient reports acute panic or anxiety.
Therapist reinforces in vivo skill use.

micro_actions.name: Prompt reflection after skill application
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to reflect on outcome (e.g., 'What effect did this have? Did you notice early signals?') after practicing skills.

name: Graded Exposure Planning and Execution
description: Therapist collaborates with patient to design exposure hierarchies and guides gradual, systematic practice facing feared situations or physical sensations.

goal.objective: Reduce avoidance and anxiety/fear response to targeted triggers through direct experience.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently completes planned exposures, demonstrates reduced avoidance and fear, and alters maladaptive beliefs.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts exposures with some anxiety but partial reduction in avoidance/fear.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids exposure tasks; maintains high anxiety and avoidance behavior.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reports successful approach behaviors toward previously avoided situations or sensations.

states: Patient identifies specific avoided situations/physical symptoms.
Patient demonstrates willingness to face or attempt exposure but needs guidance.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively identify greatest worry/catastrophic thought
micro_actions.description: Work with patient to specify the feared outcome or symptom in detail for each exposure situation.
states: Patient presents anxiety around target situations.

micro_actions.name: Guide patient to rate subjective likelihood of feared outcome
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to estimate and record odds of feared consequence occurring prior to exposure.

micro_actions.name: Design exposure tasks with patient targeting end goal
micro_actions.description: Facilitate brainstorming and planning of exposure steps; clarify specific feared result being tested.

micro_actions.name: Prompt abandonment of safety behaviors and distractions during exposure
micro_actions.description: Remind patient to refrain from using superstitious objects, safety signals, or avoidance strategies while practicing.
states: In session planning or exposure practice.

micro_actions.name: Cue use of coping skills during high anxiety moments
micro_actions.description: Instruct patient to apply breathing or thinking skills when anxiety escalates during exposure.

micro_actions.name: Support return to exposure situation after brief escape/withdrawal
micro_actions.description: Encourage patient to promptly re-enter situation after short withdrawal due to overwhelming anxiety.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate immediate and delayed reflection on exposure
micro_actions.description: Prompt the patient to reflect on outcomes and learning right after and some time after the exposure (experience vs. expectation).

micro_actions.name: Assign and review structured homework (exposure, monitoring)
micro_actions.description: Clearly communicate next steps for daily exposure practices and mood/panic monitoring forms.

name: Review, Consolidation, and Troubleshooting
description: Therapist reviews skill use and exposure outcomes with patient for consolidation, insight building, problem solving, and adjustment of strategies.

goal.objective: Consolidate learning, reinforce progress, and troubleshoot obstacles to improve future outcomes.

success_levels.ideal: Patient articulates learning, applies insights to setbacks, and shows resilience/adaptation.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient identifies some gains or obstacles, makes moderate adjustments for next steps.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient does not consolidate learning, repeats maladaptive patterns, fails to adapt strategy.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reflects on exposure/skill outcomes and proposes adjustments or acknowledges new understanding.

states: Patient completes exposure or skill application but struggles to generalize or understand results.
Therapist moves from practice to integration phase.

micro_actions.name: Prompt patient to recall and discuss daily mood and panic records
micro_actions.description: Ask about recent record entries and explore what patient noticed as outcomes and patterns.

micro_actions.name: Ask targeted questions about patterns and variability
micro_actions.description: Probe for times, places, people, and symptom variations relevant to experiences and progress.

micro_actions.name: Brainstorm methods to maintain or improve consistency
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively plan tactics with patient to address challenges in ongoing recordkeeping and skills use.

micro_actions.name: Guide patient in rating situations on hierarchy
micro_actions.description: Regularly revisit hierarchy and rate difficulty of recent/future situations (0–10 scale).
states: Patient faces new or harder situations.

micro_actions.name: Probe for unnoticed safety behaviors/avoidance patterns
micro_actions.description: Ask questions to uncover use of safety signals, objects, or avoidance the patient might miss.

micro_actions.name: Encourage objective self-focus in experience descriptions
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to describe situations factually and physically (location, sensations, actions).

micro_actions.name: Suggest seeking input from significant others about patterns
micro_actions.description: Invite patient to consult close others for direct feedback on unrecognized safety behaviors or avoidance.

name: Involvement of Significant Others and Team-Based Support
description: Therapist evaluates, coaches, and prepares significant others to provide appropriate support during exposure and coping, facilitating teamwork while minimizing rescue and reinforcement of avoidance.

goal.objective: Enhance patient progress via coordinated involvement of helpers, while increasing patient independence.

success_levels.ideal: Helpers support exposure efforts appropriately and patient transitions to independent coping.
success_levels.acceptable: Helpers are somewhat supportive; patient relies on assistance but begins practicing increased independence.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Helpers reinforce avoidance or are absent, patient remains dependent or sabotages progress.

goal.reward_hint: Patient and helpers collaborate constructively and patient progressively self-manages exposure.

states: Patient's support network can influence avoidance or progress.
Therapist discusses barriers/enablers related to significant others.
Patient demonstrates readiness or need for collaborative exposure.

micro_actions.name: Prompt patient to identify potential helpers
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to name individuals (family, friends) who could act as supporters during exposure/wellness activities.

micro_actions.name: Explore willingness and roles of identified helpers
micro_actions.description: Facilitate joint discussion with patient and helper(s) about expected roles, boundaries, and reinforcement strategies.

micro_actions.name: Model constructive exposure dialogue with helper
micro_actions.description: Demonstrate, with role play or scripting, how helpers can cue anxiety ratings and offer objective encouragement, not rescue.

micro_actions.name: Encourage use of CBT skills via helper cues
micro_actions.description: Guide helpers to prompt patient to use thinking skills or breathing exercises during anxious moments.
states: Patient and helpers discuss coping strategies.

micro_actions.name: Support pre-planning of communications for distress or withdrawal
micro_actions.description: Coach patient and helper(s) to rehearse responses to anticipated distress, aiming to maintain appropriate exposure effort.

micro_actions.name: Scaffold gradual exposure steps with team support
micro_actions.description: Adjust helper involvement in exposures over time, fostering patient independence and problem-solving as a team.

name: Medication Management and Transition Support
description: Therapist educates patient about medication use for panic/anxiety, coordinates with medical providers, and supports safe withdrawal and skill substitution.

goal.objective: Patient safely discontinues unneeded medications while maintaining progress with CBT coping skills.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes withdrawal, manages symptoms using CBT with minimal relapse.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient tapers medication, experiences mild withdrawal managed with support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient relapses or is unable to discontinue medication, coping skills are insufficient.

goal.reward_hint: Patient demonstrates safe medication reduction and relies increasingly on CBT strategies.

states: Patient is prescribed medication for panic/anxiety.
Therapist discusses treatment planning related to pharmacological support.
Patient or prescriber initiates medication tapering.

micro_actions.name: Assess patient’s current medication use and beliefs
micro_actions.description: Ask direct questions about medications, dosages, patient preferences, and attitudes towards pharmacologic treatment.

micro_actions.name: Educate on medication action, side effects, and withdrawal
micro_actions.description: Provide psychoeducation about how medications work, potential adverse effects, and process of safe withdrawal.

micro_actions.name: Prompt consultation with physician for withdrawal/taper
micro_actions.description: Remind patient to coordinate withdrawal and dosage changes directly with prescribing doctor.

micro_actions.name: Encourage gradual tapering schedule
micro_actions.description: Advise gradual reduction rather than abrupt cessation and help set a physician-approved target taper date.

micro_actions.name: Anticipate and normalize withdrawal symptoms
micro_actions.description: Discuss common withdrawal symptoms and help patient differentiate these from panic relapses, reassuring normalcy.

micro_actions.name: Coach use of CBT coping skills during withdrawal
micro_actions.description: Prompt practice of abdominal breathing, cognitive restructuring, and exposure to help manage symptoms.

micro_actions.name: Encourage self-monitoring of symptoms
micro_actions.description: Ask patient to track withdrawal symptoms and progress in diaries or on assessment forms.

micro_actions.name: Assign homework to consult physician and plan coping
micro_actions.description: Instruct patient to formally follow up with prescriber and strategize for anticipated withdrawal symptoms.

name: Maintenance Planning and Relapse Prevention
description: Therapist guides patient in developing ongoing practice plans, prepares for setbacks, problem-solves anticipated stressors, and supports long-term personal goal setting.

goal.objective: Ensure patient maintains gains, is resilient to setbacks, and self-monitors for continued progress post-therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Patient establishes and follows a maintenance plan, confidently manages future stressors with CBT skills.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient engages in some maintenance activities and copes with minor setbacks; may need booster sessions.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient has no structured plan, relapses easily when stressed, and abandons learned skills.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates personal goals, maintenance routines, and expresses readiness for self-directed progress.

states: Therapy is nearing completion or patient has achieved significant progress.
Patient expresses concern about relapse or future stressors.
Therapist wants to consolidate long-term outcomes and self-efficacy.

micro_actions.name: Assist with progress self-assessment forms
micro_actions.description: Help patient complete self-evaluation forms assessing panic, negative thoughts, and avoidance frequency/severity.
states: Therapy in maintenance or consolidation phase.

micro_actions.name: Review ratings/scales of feared situations and mood
micro_actions.description: Discuss patient’s self-report data (e.g., severity ratings around symptoms, activities, agoraphobic stimuli) and tie these to coping plans.

micro_actions.name: Provide affirmative feedback and tailored advice
micro_actions.description: Offer encouragement and specific advice based on self-evaluation and observed progress.

micro_actions.name: Help generate and update actionable practice plan
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively break down future practice into specific skills and steps, updating written plans.

micro_actions.name: Encourage periodic self-monitoring tied to life events
micro_actions.description: Prompt patient to continue regular mood/anxiety tracking alongside real-life events for consistency.

micro_actions.name: Problem-solve and mentally rehearse coping with high-risk situations
micro_actions.description: Role-play and discuss strategies for facing triggers and stressors using learned CBT skills.
states: Therapist and patient plan for setbacks.

micro_actions.name: Break down long-term goals into manageable steps
micro_actions.description: Support patient in goal setting and incremental progress tracking for maintenance.

micro_actions.name: Encourage review of psychoeducational content
micro_actions.description: Recommend regular review of anxiety/panic educational materials for ongoing learning and reinforcement.
states: Patient at risk for relapse or skill loss.
